newsitem.title: USA: Clinton vetoes tax, Medicaid items in budget pact.
newsitem.headline: Clinton vetoes tax, Medicaid items in budget pact.

text.p: President Bill Clinton used the line-item veto for the first time on Monday, striking down two tax breaks and a provision that would have reduced New York state's Medicaid expenditures.

Announcing he was vetoing the items, all part of the balanced-budget accord enacted last week, Clinton said he used the new power "to protect taxpayers and to ensure that national interests prevail over narrow interests."

The White House said Clinton's veto of a tax provision allowing financial service companies to shelter income in foreign tax havens to avoid all U.S. taxation would save the government $317 million over five years.

It said his veto of a second tax item that would have given a tax break to food processing companies that sell assets to qualified farmers' cooperatives will save the government an estimated $98 milliion over five years.

Clinton also vetoed a third provision that would have given New York state preferential treatment regarding the Medicaid health care programme for the poor, saving the federal government an estimated $200 million over five years.

"I'm hopeful that this will work out pretty much the way it did when I was (Arkansas state) governor -- that is when you know the president is prepared to use the line item veto that tends to operate as a deterrent against the most egregious kinds of project that would otherwise not be funded," Clinton said. "It would suit me if...the use of the veto became quite rare."
